When Ford announced that it would cut 800 jobs in the UK, it also criticized the government. The company said that the rules forcing car companies to sell more electric cars every year, called the zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) mandate, are "unworkable." However, back in 2022, Ford actually supported these figures and even wanted the government to raise the targets for electric car sales. They believed stronger targets would encourage customers, manufacturers, and investors to act faster.  

Female voices from Ford changed with time, showing how the group’s views shifted. They initially sang praises for the policy, but now the operation of selling electric cars is slowing down, and demand is not growing as fast as expected. The company's earlier support turned sour because market conditions have changed since the pandemic when selling any car was easier due to low interest rates.  

This situation shows the fruit of changing times and how industries need to adapt to new challenges. Even a big company like Ford can change its tune when things don’t work out as planned. P.P.S Ford’s shift in opinion highlights how tricky it can be to predict the future of car sales and electric vehicles. Any other questions?
